slides.title: 5 signs of a shady peptide seller
No certificate of analysis (COA)
slides.text: A legit seller shows a purity test result for the specific batch. No COA, or a generic one that doesn't match the batch number, is a red flag.

slides.title: Promises to treat disease
slides.text: A 'research only' product described as treating illness, reversing aging, or replacing a prescription drug breaks its own label disclaimer.

slides.title: Priced far below competitors
slides.text: A very low price often means less active substance than the label claims, or impurities - that's what independent assays of market vials have found.

list: No company address or contact details
Payment only by crypto or a personal bank transfer
